document.abstract: Despite the accelerating trend of video-source digitization, movie theaters are just beginning to introduce digital displays, and the majority still screen movies using film projectors. As a result, digital-to-film transfer is drawing attention as a key technology. To help convert film into screen-ready print, a special computer software program for moviemakers, drawing on existing color reproduction and conversion technology, has been developed. The new program, the Fuji Color Image Management System (FIMS), will now be offered to the industry as a means to transfer digital data to film.

authors.bio: Yasunori Mimaki is the North American Motion Picture Products technical assistant to the president of Fuji Photo Film U.S.A., Inc. He graduated from Tokyo Institute of Polytechnics College in 1988 with an M.S. degree in photographic engineering. Upon graduation, he joined Fuji Photo Film Co., Ltd., Ashigara Research Lab. Since then, he has worked to develop and design motion picture films. He was transferred to the U.S. in 2002.
authors.name: Yasunori Mimaki

authors.bio: Makoto Yamada is a research scientist at Ashigara Research Laboratories. He graduated from Chiba University in 1991 with an M.S. degree in image science. He began his career at Fuji Photo Film Co., Ltd., Ashigara Research Labs, in 1991. Since then, he has worked in the image design department.
